scenes.sub: Explain why a concentrated liquidity position and a grid bot are economically close cousins, and where they differ.

scenes.title: The plan
scenes.vo: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, a worked example, step by step. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.
scenes.cap: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, a worked example, step by step. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: Both strategies do the same basic thing inside a price range: sell as price rises, buy as price falls, and profit from price moving back and forth. How it trades, Discrete orders at set levels, Continuous. Every trade in range moves your inventory. What it earns, Spread between grid levels, minus exchange fees, Share of the pool's swap fee on every trade in range. Who pays whom, You pay trading fees, Traders pay you fees. At the range low, Holds mostly/all the base asset, Holds 100% of the base asset. At the range high, Holds mostly/all quote (U.S.D.T./U.S.D.C.), Holds 100% of the quote asset. Outside the range, Stops trading, holding one side, Stops earning, holding one side.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: Custody, Exchange holds funds (you keep API control), You hold keys, and the contract holds the position. Main extra risk, Exchange or counterparty, Smart contract, oracle, M.E.V., gas. Automation, Built into the tool, Manual, or a third-party manager (extra contract risk).

scenes.title: Worked example: Range $2,700–$3,300, ETH at $3,000
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Range $2,700 to $3,300, ETH at $3,000. Price falls to $2,700: geometric average the square root of (2,700 times 3,000) about $2,846. Price rises to $3,300: Almost the same inventory path. The real difference is how money is made on the way: grid profit per completed level (after paying fees), versus L.P. fee income on all trading volume in range (after impermanent loss). Grid (20 arithmetic levels, $30 apart): buys at 2,970, 2,940 … 2,700 to average buy about $2,835. Concentrated L.P.: converts U.S.D.C. to ETH continuously on the way down at the. Grid: sells at 3,030 … 3,300 to average about $3,165. L.P.: sells ETH at the square root of (3,000 times 3,300) about $3,146.
Let's look at the diagram: Grid bot versus concentrated L.P.. Take a moment with it. It's everything we've just said, in one picture.

scenes.title: Checklist
items: I can explain why both end up 100% in one asset at a range edge
I know which one pays fees and which one earns them
I treat a range break as an invalidation event in both

scenes.q: Price breaks below the range. What do the grid bot and the LP both hold?
scenes.a: All, or nearly all, the base asset, bought on the way down. Both stop earning until price returns or you act.

scenes.q: Who pays trading fees in each?
scenes.a: The grid bot pays exchange fees. The LP earns fees from traders.
scenes.vo: Question two. Who pays trading fees in each? [[pause 4]] The answer: The grid bot pays exchange fees. The L.P. earns fees from traders.

scenes.q: Name one risk the LP has that the grid bot doesn't, and vice versa.
scenes.a: LP: smart-contract/MEV/gas risk. Grid bot: exchange/counterparty risk.
